BLOCKER: reconcile --prefix + --repair is a data-loss machine: Classify filters *objects* by prefix but loads *all* metadata rows, so every row outside the prefix is classified Missing and RepairMissing DELETEs it — irreversible backup-registry loss from one well-intentioned command.

product-forge/config/residency-policy.json starts with a UTF-8 BOM (﻿); Go's encoding/json rejects BOM, so LoadRegionPolicy fails on the default path and the region guard is unusable with shipped config.
Full-service drill does not meet AC: no schema_migrations verification, no per-table checksums, and DrillReport has no RPO/archive-age field — only counts and elapsed time are recorded.

pg_dump runs without the password env: dsnEnv extracts PGPASSWORD but FullRestore never sets cmd.Env and TenantRestore discards the env entirely (`safe, _ :=`), while the password is stripped from the DSN — drills fail on any password-auth cluster, the enterprise norm; .Output() also discards stderr so failures aren't actionable.
MAJOR: --repair is destructive beyond the blocker: row-by-row DELETEs, no transaction, no dry-run listing, no audit log of what was removed, and semantics (delete metadata for *missing* objects) risk erasing legitimate records of temporarily-unlistable objects; AC wording was "repair orphaned METADATA rows" — confirm intent and add guardrails.
TenantRestore never drops the scratch DB (no defer drop as FullRestore has) — leaks databases and credentials-adjacent state on every run.
PITR check has no staleness threshold: LastArchivedAgo is reported but never evaluated, so a cluster whose last WAL archived 3 days ago still reports ok=true.
`_ = conn.QueryRow(... pg_stat_archiver).Scan(...)` swallows all errors → the tool reports "no WAL segment archived yet" instead of the real failure (fail-open on the exact signal that matters).
AC test coverage gap: no test for drill verification math, none for RepairMissing/--repair guard, none for archiver result parsing — AC explicitly requires all three.
withDB strips every query parameter (sslmode, options, search_path) when deriving scratch DSNs, so drill connections can silently run with different TLS/role semantics than production.
MINOR: run() ignores cmd.Env for all psql invocations; only pg_restore receives the password env — inconsistent auth handling across sibling commands in the same function.
withDB misbehaves on a DSN without "/" (slash == -1 → base[:0] yields a bare db name, no error).
FullRestore: dst-count failure path `continue`s before Rows accumulation; RTOOK=false does not affect the exit code, so a blown RTO budget still exits 0.
Tenant export builds `COPY (... WHERE tenant_id = '%s')` with manual quote-escaping while verification uses parameters — inconsistent injection defense; use parameterized COPY/pgx CopyFrom.
Table and scratch DB names are concatenated into SQL/DSN unquoted; repair allowlists table names but still interpolates into DELETE.
main.go: os.Exit inside deferred-output closure skips conn.Close and defers; acceptable for CLI but fragile if reused.
NIT: Classify re-filters objects by prefix even though st.List(prefix) already scopes the listing — redundant, and it's the mechanism behind the blocker.
go.sum carries testify/humanize entries for modules the package doesn't import — trim to keep dependency surface auditable.
go_modules_check.py now only expands the check set when hit ⊆ registered module names; a stray new directory under go/ silently narrows coverage — confirm intended.
residency-policy default path is CWD-relative ("config/residency-policy.json") — brittle under cron/CI; resolve relative to a known root or env.
SUMMARY: Correct shape (Go, cmd/library split, explicit exit codes, region fail-closed default) but not shippable: the prefix+repair combination can mass-delete backup metadata, the shipped policy file cannot be parsed, the drills fail on password-auth clusters, and three explicit AC elements (schema_migrations, checksums, RPO) are absent.
Top risks: destructive repair path without transaction/audit, BOM-broken guard config, and tests that skip the very verification math the AC calls out.
Recommend blocking merge until the repair path is prefix-consistent and dry-run-by-default, config parses, drills authenticate correctly, and the missing AC checks plus their tests land.
